label: Mobility types
description: How the unit moves. Each type lists the classes that may use it (this is how 'aircraft don't get tracks' is enforced), its default handling, the speeds that make sense, and what kind of target it is (a flier is in low air or high air).

terms.label: On foot
terms.description: Walks and runs. Can take cover and enter buildings and vehicles.

terms.label: Jetpack / wings
terms.description: Personal flight at low height on a jetpack or wings. Hops over walls and hovers; counts as a low flier while airborne.

terms.label: Wheels
terms.description: Fast on roads and open ground, turns in arcs, struggles on rough terrain.

terms.label: Tracks
terms.description: Slower, but turns on the spot and handles rough ground.

terms.label: Two legs
terms.description: Walks on two legs, stepping over low walls and swaying as it moves. Small ones are nimble; big ones are slow and imposing.

terms.label: Many legs
terms.description: Three or more legs, like a spider or a four-legged walker. Stable, scuttles over rubble and can straddle obstacles.

terms.label: Hover
terms.description: Air cushion or anti-grav. Crosses land and water, drifts in turns, avoids steep slopes.
terms.notes: Only for ground-level skimmers, which ground weapons hit like any vehicle. If it flies over cliffs and walls, use hovering flight (a low flier) instead.

terms.label: Hovering flight
terms.description: Rotor, VTOL or anti-grav flight. Can hover in place and strafe. Flies low, so most direct-fire weapons can reach it, not only anti-air.

terms.label: Jet
terms.description: Fixed-wing flight. Very fast, must keep moving and attacks in passes. Flies high, so only anti-air weapons reach it.

terms.label: Airship
terms.description: Lighter-than-air flight. Very slow and very tough; a looming, visible threat that flies high, so only anti-air weapons reach it.

terms.label: Ship hull
terms.description: Floats on the water surface. Research only.

terms.label: Submarine
terms.description: Moves underwater, surfacing to attack or be seen. Research only.
